page: Amazon Web Services c6i.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs and 4 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes dedicated CPU allocation with hyperthreading enabled. Memory configuration consists of 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the c6i.2xlarge consistently in the average performance tier for most compute and memory operations. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1581.0 and a multi-core score of 6011.0. Under stress-ng testing, it recorded a single-core CPU performance of 1892.79 and a multi-core performance of 7730.15. Memory bandwidth tests show 413.52 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 58.16 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

While the instance handles standard tasks like static web serving at 11.52 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 7.92 million operations per second within average parameters, it exhibits performance limitations on heavier workloads. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is rated as weak at 30.72 GB/sec. Furthermore, LLM inference benchmarks reveal a significant drop-off, with medium 7B model prompt processing scoring in the poor tier at 15.02 tokens/sec. Consequently, this instance is suited for compute-bound tasks with moderate memory requirements, such as software compilation, image processing, and web serving, rather than large-scale language model execution or memory-intensive databases.
